advantages: Returns `true` only when every element is `null` or `undefined`.
Returns `false` for empty arrays, helping distinguish “no data” from “all missing values”.
Works with `unknown[]`, making it safe to use before narrowing types.
shortDescription: Checks whether all elements in the given array are `null` or `undefined`.
typeScriptHint: Use `areNullOrUndefined` when you need to verify that an array contains only missing values (`null`/`undefined`). Note that it returns `false` for an empty array.
useCase: Validate that a list of optional fields contains no actual values (only `null`/`undefined`) before deciding to skip processing or to show a “no values provided” state.
